text:
anya: Heads-up — noticed a 15-25% p95 token latency jump on nightly canary after the kernel-selector patch (commit 9f3b2a1). Perf traces attached below.
marc: ugh. which workload? small-chat or long-context? :thinking_face:
kyle: small-chat (seq len ~64), batcher load ~180rps. I saw the spike in CI perf dashboard at 02:14 UTC. slo-monitor posted an alert.
anya: exactly small-chat. repro script: `./tools/repro.sh --profile --model llama-7b --seq 64 --rps 180`
anya: initial nvprof/nsys captures here: `gs://redwood-traces/23365/9f3b-before.nsys` and `gs://redwood-traces/23365/9f3b-after.nsys`
marc: quick diff of timelines looks like kernel selection is switching to a larger matmul kernel at runtime for many steps, incurring extra kernel swap overheads.
kyle: I loaded the before/after in perfetto and see increased kernel launch gaps ~1.2ms per step after the change. Prefetch threads also show more mutex contention.
perf-bot: git bisect started: testing range 9c1f4..9f3b2a1. current suspect 9f3b2a1.
anya: I tried forcing the old kernel policy via env `REDWOOD_KERNEL_FORCE=fast32` and p95 drops back to baseline. So selector policy likely to blame.
marc: can you paste the kernel choice snippet from the trace?
anya: copied from perfetto flame:```\nStep 0001: kernel=matmul_fast32 (exec 0.45ms)\nStep 0002: kernel=matmul_fast32 (exec 0.47ms)\nStep 0003: kernel=matmul_large (exec 1.70ms)  <-- unexpected\nStep 0004: kernel=matmul_large (exec 1.68ms)\nStep 0005: kernel=matmul_fast32 (exec 0.46ms)\n```
kyle: that jump to matmul_large every few steps matches the KV cache miss pattern I saw — when prefix cache evicts, sequence of kernels switch due to longer kv length fallback. Could be batching heuristic triggering variant probing.
marc: good call. Which batching heuristic change landed in 9f3b2a1? I recall a probe to reduce tail latency by probing larger batches.
anya: yep, PR #4121 changed probe window to 4 -> 6 and added runtime probing that temporarily switches kernel variant to test throughput. The probe apparently runs even under moderate load now.
perf-bot: bisect result: commit 9f3b2a1 introduced kernel-probe logic in selector.cpp lines 211-276.
kyle: reproducer with `--disable-probe` removes the spikes. So quick mitigation = disable probe by default until we gate it on low eviction rates.
marc: can we confirm KV eviction correlation? Any perf counters?
anya: nvprof counters: `dram_reads` spiked concurrent with kernel_large occurrences, and `L2_hit_rate` dips from 0.87 -> 0.71 during those steps. Traces: `trace://23365/kv-evict-9f3b.nsys`
kyle: also saw a higher scheduler preemption count; batcher handoff latency increased from 0.12ms -> 0.6ms during the sequences. That explains p95 overall.
anya: action plan: 1) revert the probe gate or make it conditional on kv-evictions==0, 2) add a short cooldown so we don't probe every N steps, 3) add perf unit test that runs repro and asserts p95 < baseline + 5%.
marc: agreed. For immediate rollback I've opened PR to flip default off. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4189
perf-bot: deploy preview for PR 4189 created: `canary/runtime:pr-4189`
kyle: I'll run a full nsys sweep across seq lengths {32,64,128} and both rps {50,180,400} once preview is up, then compare skyline diffs.
anya: attaching quick before/after ascii diff of kernel timeline for seq64:```\n--- before\nmatmul_fast32 x 950 steps\nmatmul_large x 30 steps\n--- after (with probe)\nmatmul_fast32 x 880 steps\nmatmul_large x 100 steps\n```
marc: thanks. Can we add logging around the probe decision? a short log with kv_cache_size, eviction_count, last_probe_ts would help debugging without full traces.
anya: on it. I'll add a debug opt-in env `REDWOOD_PROBE_DEBUG=1` that emits `PROBE_DECIDE evictions=2 cache_len=6144 chosen=large`
perf-bot: note — created perf ticket PERF-712 to track follow-up and regression test coverage.
kyle: FYI I also ran a micro-benchmark that simulates interleaved cache hits/misses; probe increased mean latency 7% under 10% eviction scenarios. Will post numbers in PERF-712.
marc: plan looks good. After PR 4189 lands, rerun CI perf job and mark regression resolved if p95 back to baseline.
anya: thanks all. I'll push the debug patch and PR 4189 now. ping me if you want to join an on-call trace session later. :eyes:
